texts: When a lantern burns mire-essence, the lantern produces mist-light.
Whenever a lantern burns mire-essence, the lantern gives mist-light.
Mist-light is a pale silver flame.
Ordinary oil does not produce mist-light.

fields.sentence: When a lantern burns mire-essence, the lantern produces mist-light.
parse: (: lantern_burn_produce (Implication (And (Member $e burn) (Agent $e $y) (Member $y lantern) (Patient $e mire_essence)) (And (Member (sk_produce $e) produce) (Agent (sk_produce $e) $y) (Patient (sk_produce $e) mist_light) (During (sk_produce $e) $e))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

review.notes: Bare "when P, Q" with an indefinite participant correctly takes the whenever/occurrence rule (premise clause, Skolem consequent, During link, STV 1.0 0.9, no QuantifierPhrase); compound genus atoms expose only the head nouns, and the inanimate transitive subject is rightly Agent.

fields.sentence: Whenever a lantern burns mire-essence, the lantern gives mist-light.
parse: (: whenever_burn_give (Implication (And (Member $x burn) (Agent $x $lantern) (Member $lantern lantern) (Patient $x mire_essence)) (And (Member (sk_give $x) give) (Agent (sk_give $x) $lantern) (Theme (sk_give $x) mist_light) (During (sk_give $x) $x))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

review.notes: Whenever-rule shape, During tie, no QuantifierPhrase companion, transitive-subject Agent, burn->Patient / give->Theme and both compound genus atoms (noun modifiers correctly unexposed) all follow the instruction set; the consequent definite 'the lantern' is correctly bound to the premise variable rather than minted as a constant.

fields.sentence: Mist-light is a pale silver flame.

q2_gaps: stacked attributive adjectives where the first grades/shades the second ('pale silver flame') — nothing licenses recording that 'pale' modifies 'silver' rather than the head noun; Degree covers only adverbial intensifiers/downtoners, and the Compound-concepts fusion tests cover adjective+noun, not adjective+adjective
review.notes: Kind subject plus Inheritance throughout, compound genus (Inheritance mist_light light) with the noun modifier 'mist' correctly unexposed, and 'pale'/'silver' correctly left unfused as incidental colour description. Definitional 0.99 on the colour properties is defensible for a stipulative fiction-world definition, though the 'when unsure -> empirical' default would give 0.9.

fields.sentence: Ordinary oil does not produce mist-light.

review.notes: Adjectivally-restricted kind subject correctly forces the distributing-rule route rather than an opaque kind relation, negated at strength 0.0 / conf 0.9, with the restriction as a premise conjunct; compound genus and the bare kind-level Patient filler follow the stated rules.
